newsitem.title: GREECE: FINANCIAL PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 10.
newsitem.headline: FINANCIAL PRESS DIGEST - GREECE - OCT 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou promises small and medium-size enterprises (SMEs) that an amendment freeing up rentals on business premises will be ready by the end of the month.
--Contract between National Bank and Calcestruzzi over Aget-Heracles cement company imminent. New agreement will give National a 32 percent stake in Aget.
--State titles will not be taxed. Government appears reluctant, for the moment, to make the move.
--Tourism research institute optimistic about the course of the economy next year, but drachma and income policies must change.
--Slight increase in industrial production in June, national statistics service says.
--Bank of Crete presents profits of 1.1 billion in first half 1996.
IMERISIA
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis to call for social and political consensus on the critical situation of the Greek economy when he presents policy statements in Parliament today.

--Despite difficulties, Simitis optimistic about the course of inflation and interest rates. Simitis is expected to stress to Parliament that the consumer price index (CPI) can fall below 5 percent next year.

--Alpha Credit and Labour Banks examining prospects of joint business activity, according to internal Credit Bank document. --Aluminium de Grece announces a 17 billion drachma investment plan for the next five-year period in a bid to improve competitiveness.
KERDOS
--Markets refuse to give Simitis government a honeymoon and want the government to move speedily ahead with development initiatives and stabilisation policies.
--Two leaders in Greek venture capital market invest in health services sector. Global Finance and Commercial Capital buy into Thessaloniki health clinic.
--Contract for new Rhodes casino signed yesterday with consortium in which Mihaniki (33 percent), Commercial Bank subsidiary 'Enias' (33 percent) and Playboy (16 percent) are participating.
EXPRESS
--Today is the day measures and the road to convergence are announced. Emphasis expected to fall on containing deficits, state sector and income increases in the order of inflation.
--1995 tax revenues meet expectations. Objective tax criteria caused an increase in declared incomes, finance ministry says.
--Back to work on the Metro. Meeting between Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis and Olympic Metro representatives overcome stumbling blocks at yesterday's meeting.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--Investment opportunities for Greek firms in Russia. Simitis in Moscow later this month as Russians aim for joint ventures in various sectors and hope to get contracts to replace Greek trolleys and hyrdofoil fleets.
--Average tax burden for all business categories up, according to finance ministry figures.
